abstract: Aniridia-associated keratopathy (AAK), caused by PAX6 haploinsufficiency, progresses from a clinically clear cornea to opacity, neovascularization, and abnormal innervation, but when disease-associated changes first emerge remains unclear. We combined corneal nerve imaging, CD31 immunolabeling, transmission electron microscopy, and RNA sequencing of whole cornea from Pax6Sey-Neu/+mice at postnatal day 3-4, day 15, and adulthood. Corneal transcripts were analyzed using curated axon-guidance, myelination, and vascular/lymphatic gene panels. Mutant corneas showed reduced nerve density and persistent stromal fascicles beginning during the first postnatal week. Peripheral vascular structures were present in both genotypes at birth; these resolved during normal maturation but persisted and extended centrally in mutant corneas by two weeks, before loss of transparency. Transcriptomic analysis identified widespread differences between genotypes while both corneas remained transparent, with the strongest and most coherent changes involving vascular and lymphatic genes. Wild-type corneas silenced an endothelial and lymphatic expression program between postnatal day 15 and adulthood, whereas mutant corneas retained expression of this program. Individual axon-guidance genes differed between genotypes, but axon-guidance did not show program-level expansion in transparent corneas. Compact stromal myelin was restricted to opaque regions. These findings identify early vascular and neural abnormalities that precede corneal opacity and establish that a transparent Pax6-haploinsufficient cornea is already pathologically altered.
